# Vendored librespot crates

Copies of published librespot 0.8.0 crates (MIT licensed, see `LICENSE` in each
directory), wired into the build through `[patch.crates-io]` in
`native/Cargo.toml`. Every local change is marked with a `// SPOTIFYGOOD:`
comment so the patch can be re-applied when upgrading librespot.

| Crate | Why it is vendored |
|-------|--------------------|
| `librespot-core` | Stock `Session::check_catalogue` calls `std::process::exit(1)` for non-Premium accounts, which would kill the Android app. It is patched to report the error and shut the session down instead. |
| `librespot-connect` | The stock crate keeps the Connect state private. The app needs to read the queue and context, edit the queue locally, see the other Connect devices in the account, and implement smart shuffle. |
| `librespot-playback` | Offline playback of downloaded (still encrypted) tracks needs a hook in the track loader; the stock player also calls `exit(1)` on sink errors, gives no way to tell refused audio keys apart, and runs one tokio worker per CPU core. See `librespot-playback/PATCHES.md`. |

## Patches

`grep -rn SPOTIFYGOOD native/vendor` lists every change. Files that are entirely
new say so in their first line.

### librespot-core

| File | What | Why |
|------|------|-----|
| `src/session.rs` | `check_catalogue` is now a method. For a non-Premium `type` attribute it records `SessionInvalidReason::NonPremiumAccount { account_type }` and calls `Session::shutdown()` instead of `std::process::exit(1)`. It covers the ProductInfo packet and `set_user_attribute(s)`. Adds `pub enum SessionInvalidReason` (`#[non_exhaustive]`) and `pub fn Session::invalid_reason(&self) -> Option<SessionInvalidReason>`. Removes the `process::exit` import. | `exit(1)` would kill the Android app and its foreground service without any UI. |
| `src/config.rs` | `pub const OS: &str = "linux"` (was `std::env::consts::OS`). `os_version()` falls back to `"6.1"` when sysinfo returns nothing or an empty string (was `"0"`). | On `target_os = "android"`, librespot presents the Android-app identity, and Spotify rejects that identity for keymaster-minted credentials. Every platform branch in core matches on this const, so the whole crate now presents the Linux desktop identity: the default client id is keymaster (`SessionConfig::default`, login5), the client-token platform data is `desktop_linux`, the user agent is `Spotify/<desktop version> Linux/0`, the AP handshake uses `PLATFORM_LINUX_*` / `OS_LINUX`, and `spotify_version()` is the desktop one. There are no direct `cfg(target_os)` or `consts::OS` uses in core. Consequence: `Login5Manager::login` (password login) returns `OnlyForMobile`, which the app doesn't use. spotify-player's Termux build applies the same patch. |
| `src/spclient.rs` | `pub fn RequestOptions::new(metrics: bool, salt: bool, base_url: Option<&'static str>) -> Self`. The fields stay private. | Without it, callers outside the crate can only use the default options with `request_with_options` (metrics and salt on). |
| `src/dealer/mod.rs` | In the reconnect loop, a failing `get_url()` (login5/apresolve) is logged, waits `RECONNECT_INTERVAL` (10 s) and retries, unless the dealer is closed. Before, the `?` ended the dealer for good. The connect-error sleep also aborts on close. | A transient token failure silently killed Connect for the rest of the session. `Dealer::close` no longer waits out the 10 s delay. |
| `src/audio_key.rs` | `AudioKeyError::AesKey { code: u16 }` (was a unit variant), parsed as a big-endian u16 from the `AesKeyError` payload after the sequence number, with no panic on a short payload. Display: `audio key error 0x0001`. Adds `pub const AES_KEY_ERROR_PERMANENT: u16 = 0x0001` and `AES_KEY_ERROR_TRANSIENT: u16 = 0x0002`. Code `0x0001` maps to `ErrorKind::PermissionDenied`, all other codes and `Timeout` map to `ErrorKind::Unavailable` (`Timeout` was `Aborted`). Adds `pub fn is_permanent_denial(err: &Error) -> bool`. The pending sender is removed on timeout and when sending the request fails (it leaked before). Adds a unit test. | Spotify refuses audio keys for some accounts (librespot #1649 / PR #1763). Callers (the vendored playback) need to tell "refused for this account" apart from throttling. |
| `src/dealer/protocol/request.rs` | **Unchanged.** serde ignores unknown fields (there is no `deny_unknown_fields` anywhere), so a `set_options` with extra fields such as `modes` still parses. A connect test covers this. Note that a present `options` object needs all three `OptionsOptions` bools. | Checked, no change needed. |

### librespot-connect

| File | What | Why |
|------|------|-----|
| `Cargo.toml` | tokio features `rt` and `time` are now listed. | `tokio::spawn` (suggestion fetches), `sleep` and `timeout`. Before, these only worked through feature unification with core. |
| `src/snapshot.rs` (new), `src/lib.rs` | Public read-only types `ConnectSnapshot` (with `ending`, see A), `SnapshotTrack`, `TrackProvider`, `SnapshotPlayStatus` and `SpircCommandError`. | The app needs the state, which upstream keeps private. |
| `src/state/snapshot.rs` (new) | `ConnectState::snapshot()` builds the snapshot. `can_skip_prev` is true whenever a track is current: without a previous track, previous restarts it, so the restriction reason "no previous tracks" alone doesn't disable it (it did on the first track of a load and after every shuffle). `snapshot_fingerprint()` is a cheap hash, so Spirc skips the rebuild when nothing visible changed. The position is hashed as its nominal start while playing, so re-anchoring on each PUT doesn't count as a change. | Snapshot stream (A). |
| `src/spirc.rs` | **A** `subscribe_state()`. A `watch` channel, published with `send_if_modified` at the bottom of every loop iteration and once in `Spirc::new`. The final snapshot, sent after the epilogue, has `ending: true` and is the state when the loop ended, before the epilogue's disconnect (a task that ended by itself would otherwise report "stopped, inactive" and hide what was playing). `is_running()` tells whether the task still takes commands: the channel is closed as soon as the loop ends (it stayed open for the whole epilogue), and a `Shutdown` left in it is still honoured (the player is paused). **B** `add_to_queue`, `remove_from_queue`, `move_queue_item`, `clear_queue`, `skip_to` (active only). `add_to_queue` fails right away (FailedPrecondition, `StateError::QueueFull`) when the queued tracks plus the adds not handled yet fill the 80 next tracks (a shared gauge, kept by the task); the task checks again, and the remote `add_to_queue` endpoint now fails instead of dropping the track. After every queue change, local or remote (`add_to_queue`/`set_queue`), and after shuffle changes, the next track is preloaded again if a preload had already been triggered. **C** `subscribe_cluster()` publishes `Option<Arc<Cluster>>` from the NEW_DEVICE PUT, from every cluster push, and from state/volume/audio-output PUT responses that parse as a cluster with devices. `refresh_cluster()` (allowed while inactive) puts the state to get a fresh cluster; a failure is only logged. **D** `smart_shuffle(bool)`. Suggestions are fetched off the loop (`tokio::spawn` + `get_autoplay_context` with about 20 sampled context track uris, bounded by 20 s), at most one request at a time, and delivered back through a new `select!` arm. The request is aborted when its result becomes invalid and when the task ends (also when its future is dropped), so it never keeps the session alive. Results are dropped if the generation or context changed. Pacing: 30 s minimum between fetches, 5 min after an empty result, 30 s doubling to 10 min on errors, at most 40 pending suggestions. Suggestions are refetched after a load, a reshuffle, or a change to the default context through the resolver. **E** `set_audio_output(kind, name)`, allowed while inactive, PUTs with `AUDIO_DRIVER_INFO_CHANGED` only when the value changed. **F** Shutdown sets the flags first and never fails. The disconnect and the epilogue's DELETE and dealer close are each bounded by 3 s. A closed command channel (all handles dropped) is treated as shutdown, and a closed player event channel stops being polled (both were busy loops). No handler awaits a state put any more (`StatePuts`): every command, the remote transfer, the activation, `refresh_cluster`, `set_audio_output` (AUDIO_DRIVER_INFO_CHANGED), the volume puts, the put after a resolve and the delayed background put only request one. At most one put is in flight, bounded by 5 s and polled by the loop next to the commands and player events; the ones requested meanwhile wait, at most one of each kind, and are built when sent (so they carry the state of then). The handlers used to await their put without a bound (spclient retries and sleeps out a 429's Retry-After), so a pause (headphones unplugged, a call) or the end of a track waited behind the put of the previous command, for up to a minute. A put failure is logged, not reported as the command's failure (the command was applied). A put that times out or fails transiently is sent again after 2 s and then 10 s (with the state of then), unless a newer put of its kind supersedes it, then it is given up; it used to be dropped, so Spotify and the other devices kept the old state (e.g. still playing after a pause) until some later put. A disconnect, an inactive state and a connection id update (NEW_DEVICE) drop the puts in flight or waiting first, so that none lands after them. The two requests of `handle_disconnect` stay awaited, each bounded by 5 s (the local state becomes inactive either way); the transfer request of an inactive device is bounded by 10 s; every context fetch is bounded by 10 s (`ContextResolver::get_next_context`, a load awaits the first one). The NEW_DEVICE put that announces the device (its response is the first cluster) is bounded by 30 s; the task then ends like after a failed dealer setup (a live task never delivered its first cluster). `Drop for SpircTask` pauses the player unless spirc stopped it: a task that ended by itself, or was aborted in the middle of a handler (so `handle_shutdown` never ran), left it playing. Commands are now always polled: anything other than `Shutdown` that arrives before the connection is established is buffered, so an early shutdown no longer hangs. That includes the dealer start before the loop: it is raced against `Shutdown` (which ends the task right away) and bounded by 30 s (the task then ends, like after a failed start). **G** `ConnectConfig.auto_takeover` gates the startup takeover. The takeover restores playback paused (`handle_transfer(.., start_paused)`). **I** `last_error` in the snapshot, plus `subscribe_errors()` (`broadcast`, capacity 16). Commands that are ignored while inactive now report `NotActive` (FailedPrecondition). **J** Cluster update without a cluster while active also stops the player, and so does the transfer-away branch (another device became active); both stop it before their requests (it played on until they gave up), publish the snapshot as inactive and stopped before the (bounded) requests, so that commands follow the device that took over instead of queueing behind the requests and being dropped as not active, and forget the request id. `handle_disconnect` becomes inactive even if the state update fails (it returned early, so the device kept reporting itself as active). `prev` with repeat and no prev tracks loads the track; without repeat it restarts the current track (it stopped playback). FilterExplicitContentChanged is emitted for both values. A remote `skip_next` to a uri that isn't in the next tracks falls back to a plain next, where before it consumed the queue, stopped playback, or never ended. **K** `set_autoplay(bool)` sets the local `autoplay` user attribute. It fails when `SessionConfig.autoplay` overrides it. Once set, the local value wins: `attributes:mutated` for autoplay is ignored (it used to flip the local value, which no longer mirrors the account), `attributes:update` keeps it, and Spirc reads the local value even if the attributes are replaced. Enabling queues an autoplay resolve; disabling drops pending autoplay resolves and the autoplay context unless autoplay is already playing. **M** An inactive spirc ignores all player events: the app's offline playback drives the same player, and an inactive spirc used to adopt those request ids and stop the player at the end of every offline track. `release_player()` hands the player back to the app once it detached the spirc: the task stops handling events (it shuts down at once) and never drives the player again (no load, play, pause, seek, preload or stop, also not from a handler that was waiting on a request, its shutdown or `Drop`): the app's offline playback may already run on it, and the app pauses what the detached spirc played. A load from a uri asks the resolver again even if the same context failed a moment ago, and only a context that can't be resolved (not found, not allowed, invalid) is skipped for a while; a transient failure (network, rate limit, server error) used to refuse that context without any request for 60 s. **L** `PlayerEvent::Unavailable` uses the reason: transient failures (`KeyTemporarilyDenied`, `NetworkError`) don't mark the track unavailable for the session (it is skipped, not blacklisted), and a failed preload only preloads the following track for track-specific reasons. After a key denial or a transient failure the chain of preloads walked the whole queue with one key request per track while a track played; that track is now loaded, and its failure handled, when the current one ends. **N** Play and play/pause while stopped but active (the context ended, or the player was halted after refused loads) play the current track again from its start, like the remote resume; without a current track they fail (`NothingToPlay`, FailedPrecondition). They were ignored and reported success (`play_action`). **P** A resolve of the loop that fails is retried, and the state is still set up when it fails for good (see `src/context_resolver.rs`); the resolve a load waits for isn't retried, the load reports the failure. A given up resolve of the default context marks it incomplete, so a load of it resolves it again; a load skips the resolve only for a context that is resolved and all there. **O** A load that resets the context completely (another uri, or a track list) drops the resolves and the transfer still pending for the previous context (`reset_context` tells it). Only a load of another uri did: after a track list load, the album pages of an artist played a moment before were appended to the new list, and they deferred its shuffle. | See the items in `connect.md` §15. |
| `src/state.rs` | `ConnectConfig.auto_takeover` (default false). `send_with_reason` PUTs a copy of the request carrying the reason (cancel safe: a timed-out PUT left the reason set for every later PUT). `reset_playback_to_position` sets the fill up page to the pass of the current track (it started over at 0), forgets the played smart shuffle suggestions and keeps the waiting ones (the one after the track it continues after is inserted first, the fill up starts behind it). `SPOTIFY_MAX_NEXT_TRACKS_SIZE` is `pub(crate)`, `StateError::QueueFull`. New state: `skipped_uids`, `smart_shuffle`, `suggestions`, `used_suggestion_uris`. `set_audio_output()`. `put_state_request(reason)` (a copy of the request for Spirc's state puts; `notify_volume_changed` is gone). `StateError::CanNotFindTrackInQueue`. `reset_playback_to_position` keeps a track that isn't part of the context (queued, a playing suggestion, or removed by a context update) as the current track. Its index is then the context track that track follows (the fill up continues after it, it is the last prev track); without an index the context starts over at its first track (upstream skipped that one). `keeps_current_track()` tells such a track apart. | B, D, E, G |
| `src/state/handle.rs` | `queue_add_uri` (validated through `SpotifyUri`), `queue_remove`, `queue_clear`, `queue_move`, `clear_skipped_uids`, `has_playable_next_track`, `remove_autoplay_context`. Unshuffle and the repeat-context toggle work out where the playback continues before they change anything: after the current track, the track a playing suggestion follows, or the last context track played before a queued track, else before the first upcoming one (`playback_anchor`). They used to look a queued track up by uri and failed half applied, or jumped to the same song elsewhere in the context. Unshuffling clears smart shuffle; while autoplay plays it only unshuffles the played default context. The repeat-context toggle is refused while autoplay plays. Shuffle on is validated before the option changes, and refused while autoplay is the active context (`validate_shuffle_toggle`, also for smart shuffle): it started the played default context over, then replayed the autoplay tracks. Invariant: queued tracks stay contiguous at the front. | B, D, J, K |
| `src/state/tracks.rs` | `next_tracks_mut` is now `pub(super)`. `add_to_queue` returns `Result` and fails when 80 queued tracks fill the next tracks (the track was pushed and popped right away). Dropping the end of the next tracks (`add_to_queue`, `prev_track`) rewinds the fill up to the earliest dropped context or autoplay track (by uid, also when shuffled; a dropped delimiter wraps or transitions to autoplay again), so the dropped tracks are played later; upstream lost them. `prev_track` puts the old track and a delimiter back after the queued tracks, not in front of them. The fill up stores its pass (`index.page`, counting repeat wraps) instead of starting every later fill up at the stored page again (delimiter uids repeated, `refill_next_tracks` already assumed it was stored); `current_pass()` is the pass of the current track (the iteration of the first delimiter in the next tracks, else the stored page). A context track with a suggestion goes in only together with it: with one free slot the fill up stops before it (the next tracks then hold 79), and a suggestion dropped from the end takes its context track along, so the size cap never loses a suggestion. `prev_track` sets the index from the track's `context_index` instead of decrementing blindly. `clear_next_tracks` rewinds the autoplay fill up to the first autoplay track it drops (a later transition skipped them). Without a previous track `prev_track` returns `None` and changes nothing (it moved the current track to the next tracks and left the state without one), so Spirc can restart the track. `skip_to_uid` is added. `truncate_next_tracks` is `pub(super)`. | B, D |
| `src/state/transfer.rs` | A transferred queue stops at the first track `add_to_queue` rejects (full queue). A shuffled transfer keeps a queued current track, or one the context doesn't contain (`keeps_current_track`), as the current track; it was replaced by a context track, so the state named another song than the one playing. `handle_initial_transfer` leaves the context (its pages) in the transfer, `finish_transfer_without_context` makes the default context of them (or of the current track) when the context can't be resolved, and marks it incomplete. | B |
| `src/state/restrictions.rs` | Toggling repeat-context and shuffle is also disallowed while a queued track plays after the default context ended (autoplay is the active context); `handle_set_repeat_context` and turning shuffle or smart shuffle on refuse it then. `NO_PREV` is module level (for `can_skip_prev`). | B |
| `src/state/smart_shuffle.rs` (new) | Local smart shuffle. Suggestions are keyed by the pass through the default context (`index.page`, the wraps with repeat) and the position in the shuffled default context after which they are inserted (one after every 3rd context track, continuing into the following passes with repeat, up to the end of the context without), so each one is inserted once and are never added to `StateContext.tracks`, so unshuffle keeps working. They keep the `context` provider, carry the metadata `smart_shuffle.suggested=true`, and take the `context_index` of the track they follow. Already-suggested uris and uris of the context are filtered out. Without repeat, suggestions for later passes are dropped (a stale one blocked every new batch). | D |
| `src/state/metadata.rs`, `src/state/options.rs`, `src/state/context.rs`, `src/model.rs` | Suggestion metadata key. `validate_shuffle_allowed` is now `pub(super)`. `shuffle_new` puts no context track first (and skips none in the first pass) while the current track isn't part of the context; the same song elsewhere in the context was skipped. `reset_context(Completely)` clears the skipped uids and smart shuffle, and `reset_context` returns whether it reset completely. "The same context" (`WhenDifferent`, `is_current_context`) is only a context that was resolved and is all there: not without a context (a transfer still resolving it) and not one marked incomplete (`mark_default_context_incomplete`: the stand-in of a failed transfer, or a resolve of it or of one of its pages failed for good; a real resolve clears it). A load of such a uri ran on what was there (the tapped song wasn't found, the first one played) or failed with NoContext, and it was never resolved again until another context played. An update of the same context (a playlist modification) continues after the current track, else at the first upcoming context track, else after the last played one, matched by uid (`position_in_context`, else by uri). It used `fill up index - 80`, which replayed tracks once queued tracks rewound the fill up and skipped them otherwise. The update also switches the fill up back to the default context (it lost the rest of the default context once the fill up was in autoplay), keeps the pass, and leaves the next tracks alone while autoplay plays (they were cleared, and the playback stopped after the current track). `fill_context_from_page(page, ty)` appends to the context of the given type (the Append arm of `ContextResolver::apply_next_context` passes the type of the resolve, `update_context` its own). Upstream always appended to the default context, also the further pages and the Append resolves of autoplay: the autoplay context never grew, so autoplay stopped after its first batch, and the playlist got the autoplay tracks as its own. Autoplay tracks that are already there are skipped. Pages appended to the default context while it is already shuffled (shuffle on while its pages still resolve) go through `ShuffleVec::extend_keep_shuffle`, so shuffle off restores the context order (it left the first page shuffled). Before a further page of the playing default context is appended, the next tracks past the end of the context so far are dropped (the wraps of repeat, or the transition to autoplay; the fill up rewinds to the end in the same pass), so the new tracks come next: the 10 top tracks of an artist wrapped about 7 times before its albums played. `update_context` appends its own further pages without that (`append_page`). An update of the context that plays shuffled keeps its order (`keep_shuffle_on_update`): the tracks played in this pass stay first, the upcoming ones keep their order, added tracks go to random places among them, and removed ones are gone. The seed, the pass and the prev tracks stay, and unshuffle gives the order of the updated context. This applies only when all its pages carry their tracks; otherwise it is shuffled from scratch, as before. `Options.smart_shuffle` (implies shuffle). `AudioOutputKind` maps to the proto `AudioOutputDeviceType`. | B, D, E |
| `src/context_resolver.rs` | The retry of unavailable contexts was dead code because the `duration_since` arguments were swapped; this is fixed. `RETRY_UNAVAILABLE` drops from 3600 s to 60 s. `get_next_context` is bounded by 10 s (DeadlineExceeded, transient: the context isn't marked unavailable); a load sent just before the network died hung the Spirc loop. A resolve of the loop that fails transiently is kept and fetched again after 2, 5 and 10 s (`retry_next_later`, the wait is absolute, so a fetch the loop restarts doesn't start it over). One that fails for good still sets the state up when it was the last of its kind (`finish_after_failure`, factored with `try_finish` into `last_of_kind`): a pending transfer is finished (with a context made of the tracks it brought, or of its current track), the shuffle a load deferred runs on the pages there are, otherwise the next tracks are filled. A failed resolve was dropped: the transfer never finished (no next tracks, its queue lost) and the deferred shuffle never ran, so the playback stopped after the current track. Adds `remove_autoplay()` and `next_update()`. Adds `forget_unavailable()` (an explicit load always reaches the network) and `is_unavailable(error)` (which failures mark a context unavailable, see M). The further pages (`page_url`) of a context keep its type: an autoplay context's pages are resolved like a context page and appended to the autoplay context (they went into the default context). Only these page follow-ups (marked `page`) are fetched as context pages; every other resolve goes by its type, so the autoplay continuation (an Append of the playing context) keeps asking the autoplay endpoint with the played tracks. An append accepts a page with several track pages (every one with tracks is appended; it failed with `UnexpectedPagesSize`). `try_finish` doesn't shuffle the context again after an update (Replace) of the context that already played shuffled: `update_context` kept its order. Notes for users of the connect patches:
- Snapshot clock: `position_timestamp_ms` is local epoch milliseconds (the same clock as `System.currentTimeMillis()`). The position now is `position_ms + (now - position_timestamp_ms) * playback_speed`, and `playback_speed` is 0 unless the status is `Playing`. Internally, Spirc puts server-corrected timestamps (`local + time_delta`).
- `next_tracks` and `prev_tracks` include hidden delimiters (`hidden == true`, uri `spotify:delimiter`). Filter them out for display.
- Only `subscribe_*`, `is_running`, `set_audio_output`, `set_autoplay`, `refresh_cluster`, `activate`, `transfer` and `shutdown` work while the device is inactive. Every other command reports a `NotActive` error. To control another device, use spclient directly.
- Smart shuffle is local. Other clients see the suggestions as ordinary context tracks, and the mode is not sent to Spotify (`modes` is not set).
